description: Every hexa project provides agent orientation via AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, roles, skills, and module READMEs.

accepted.by: gary (standing instruction: always accept the ADRs and specs; the owner asked for this work on 2026-11-22; recorded by the implementing agent)

specs.description: hexa init writes AGENTS.md with the managed section.
specs.when: hexa init is run on it.
specs.then: AGENTS.md exists with the hexa-managed section between `<!-- hexa:agents-md:start -->` and `<!-- hexa:agents-md:end -->`, holding Start here, Where builds run, Find your place and the shipped guide (`hexa do gate`, `hexa graph context`).

specs.description: An AGENTS.md without markers keeps its text and gets the section appended
specs.given: An initialised project whose AGENTS.md is hand-written text with no hexa markers.
specs.then: The hand-written text is the unchanged prefix of the file, and the managed section follows it, once; a second refresh changes nothing.

specs.given: An initialised project whose CLAUDE.md has the claude-md markers around an old body with no `@AGENTS.md`.
specs.then: The managed section holds the line `@AGENTS.md` and the Claude-only parts (hooks, skills, `.claude/agents/`), and does not repeat AGENTS.md's verb table.

specs.description: A CLAUDE.md with no hexa section is never appended to
specs.given: An initialised project whose CLAUDE.md is hand-written with no markers and no legacy hexa heading.
specs.then: CLAUDE.md is byte-for-byte unchanged, and refresh says it has no hexa-managed section.

specs.description: refresh replaces only the managed section.
specs.given: An initialised project whose AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md each have hand-written text above and below the markers, and a stale body between them.
specs.then: Only the bytes between the markers are replaced, and hand-written text is unchanged.

specs.description: refresh refuses files with end marker before start marker.
specs.given: An initialised project whose AGENTS.md has the end marker before the start marker.
specs.then: The command fails, names AGENTS.md, and the file is unchanged.

specs.description: hexa init installs the lead role, builder role, and parallel-agents skill.
specs.then: `.claude/agents/hexa-lead.md`, `.claude/agents/hexa-builder.md` and `.claude/skills/hexa-parallel-agents/SKILL.md` exist, and between them name: cargo fmt before push; wait on your own remote run and never end the turn mid-run; counts only from the remote run on the pushed head; one writer per branch; generated files only through their tool; never restart a CI runner with a job in flight; split by file; integrate, never trust.

specs.description: skill sync restores a deleted role and leaves an edited one alone
specs.given: An initialised project where `.claude/agents/hexa-lead.md` was deleted and `.claude/agents/hexa-builder.md` was edited.
specs.then: hexa-lead.md is written back with the shipped bytes; the edited hexa-builder.md is unchanged and named as differing.

specs.when: hexa init --scaffold is run on it (rust).
specs.then: Each layer directory the scaffold wrote (`src/domain`, `src/ports`, `src/usecases`, `src/adapters`) holds a README.md with `## Owns`, `## May import`, `## Tests` and `## ADRs`, and its May import names that layer's rule.

specs.description: docs check flags a module without a README, and docs readmes writes it back
specs.given: A scaffolded project whose `src/ports/README.md` was removed.
specs.when: hexa docs check --json is run, then hexa docs readmes.
specs.then: docs check reports a `missing_module_readme` finding for `src/ports`; after docs readmes the file exists again and docs check reports none, and an existing README is not overwritten.

specs.description: doctor reports failing checks with fix commands.
specs.given: An initialised project with AGENTS.md removed, a shipped skill removed, the hook commands removed from .claude/settings.json, and a module README removed.
specs.then: It names each missing piece with its fix (`hexa refresh`, `hexa skill sync`, `hexa refresh`, `hexa docs readmes`), reports the graph as fresh, stale, missing or unknown (`hexa graph build` when stale or missing), and exits non-zero.

specs.description: finish lists failing orientation checks, only in an initialised project
specs.given: An initialised project with AGENTS.md removed; and a repository with `.hexa/` but no `.hexa/project.json`.
specs.when: hexa finish --json and hexa finish --exit-code are run in each.
specs.then: The first lists an `orientation` item naming AGENTS.md with fix `hexa refresh` and exits 1; the second lists no `orientation` item.

specs.description: AGENTS.md's managed section is always wrapped in the correct markers.
specs.when: wrap is called with AGENTS_MD markers.
specs.then: The result is the body text wrapped between the start and end markers, each on its own line.

specs.description: imports_agents_md returns true only for the exact import line.
specs.then: It returns true if and only if the text contains a line that is exactly '@AGENTS.md' outside a code fence.

specs.description: module_readme always includes the four headings.
specs.then: The result is a string containing '## Owns', '## May import', '## Tests', and '## ADRs'.

specs.description: graph_state returns Fresh only for the exact 'fresh' state.
specs.given: Any JSON string from hexa graph status --json.
specs.then: It returns Fresh for state `fresh`, Stale for `stale`, Missing for `missing`, and Unknown for no output, invalid JSON, or any other state.

specs.description: replace_managed changes only the managed bytes and is idempotent
specs.given: Any prefix and suffix without markers, any old body and any new body.
specs.when: replace_managed is applied to prefix + wrapped(old) + suffix, then again to its result.
specs.then: The result starts with the prefix and ends with the suffix unchanged, its managed body is the new body, and the second application returns the same text; text with no markers returns None; end-before-start is an error.

specs.description: Every shipped role and the skill are project-neutral
specs.then: It names no project-specific host, crate or script of the project it was derived from (datum, tt, max, bazzite, ci/remote-gate.sh, cargo xtask), and every `hexa` verb it names exists.
